statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study followed 23 children being treated for atopic dermatitis to track how their colonizing S. aureus changed over time.
statements.evidence: by longitudinally tracking 23 children treated for AD
statements.note: The cohort was 23 children treated for AD, followed longitudinally to watch S. aureus adapt.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In reanalyzed genomes, capD negativity was more common among atopic dermatitis isolates than in other settings.
statements.evidence: capD negativity is more common in AD than in other contexts
statements.note: Reanalysis of 276 people's genomes showed capD negativity occurs more often in AD than elsewhere.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Clearing S. aureus from the skin with antibiotics reverses atopic dermatitis severity in these children.
statements.evidence: worsens disease severity by promoting skin damage
statements.note: The abstract links S. aureus to worse AD but never tests whether removing it reverses severity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within each patient a single S. aureus lineage prevailed, and distant lineages invaded only infrequently.
statements.evidence: Each patient's S. aureus population is dominated by a single lineage, with infrequent invasion by distant lineages
statements.note: Each patient carried one dominant lineage, invaded only rarely by genetically distant lineages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The researchers analyzed chromosome-level genome assemblies from three representative Cyanidiophyceae species to study their genomic adaptation.
statements.evidence: chromosome-level assemblies from three representative Cyanidiophyceae species
statements.note: Three chromosome-level Cyanidiophyceae assemblies were analyzed to probe genomic adaptation to extreme habitats.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cyanidiophyceae red algae have persisted in hot springs and related sites worldwide for more than one billion years.
statements.evidence: has successfully thrived in hot springs and associated sites worldwide for more than 1 billion years
statements.note: These red algae have occupied hot springs globally for over a billion years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most adaptive genes, including those for arsenic detoxification, arose independently in the Cyanidiales and Galdieriales lineages.
statements.evidence: most of the adaptive genes (e.g., for arsenic detoxification) evolved independently in these lineages
statements.note: Although both orders face similar stress, most adaptive genes evolved separately in each lineage.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The horizontal gene transfers in these algae originated mainly from bacteria sharing the same hot-spring habitats.
statements.evidence: in addition to horizontal gene transfer events
statements.note: The abstract credits horizontal gene transfer in adaptation but never identifies the donor organisms.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The loss of IFN-α genes leaves bats more vulnerable to bacterial infections of the skin.
statements.evidence: This shift to IFN-ω could contribute to the increased viral tolerance
statements.note: The abstract ties the interferon shift to viral tolerance, saying nothing about bacterial infection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The long-read assemblies revealed a contraction of interferon-α at the type I IFN locus, shifting relative IFN-ω and IFN-α copy numbers.
statements.evidence: revealed a contraction of interferon (IFN)-α at the immunity-related type I IFN locus in bats
statements.note: Long-read assemblies showed interferon-α shrank at the type I IFN locus, altering IFN-ω/IFN-α ratios.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the bat genomes, 33 tumor suppressor genes and 6 DNA-repair genes carried signatures of positive selection.
statements.evidence: 33 tumor suppressors and 6 DNA-repair genes showed signs of positive selection
statements.note: Thirty-three tumor suppressors and six DNA-repair genes bore marks of positive selection in bats.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Three bat species had lost all of their IFN-α genes, contrary to earlier ideas of constitutive IFN-α expression.
statements.evidence: three bat species lost all IFN-α genes
statements.note: Contrary to the constitutive-IFN-α hypothesis, three bat species had lost every IFN-α gene.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The model inferred a recent sixfold increase in population size, alongside a fitness-effect distribution skewed toward effectively neutral mutations.
statements.evidence: inferred a recent 6-fold population growth together with a distribution of fitness effects that is skewed towards effectively neutral mutations
statements.note: Analysis inferred recent sixfold growth and a fitness-effect distribution dominated by near-neutral mutations.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Balancing selection was detected at specific immune loci in the Yoruba genome.
statements.evidence: essential for identifying candidate loci experiencing relatively rare and episodic forms of selection (e.g., positive or balancing selection)
statements.note: Balancing selection is named only as a target the baseline helps find, not a result reported here.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The baseline model was built for the Yoruba, a West African population, from processes acting continuously on the genome.
statements.evidence: a baseline model was developed for a human population of West African ancestry, the Yoruba
statements.note: Supported: the model was developed specifically for the Yoruba from constantly operating genomic processes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Strong or frequent recurrent positive selection was inconsistent with the data, whereas weak-to-moderate positive selection stayed consistent but undetectable when rare.
statements.evidence: although strong and/or frequent recurrent positive selection is inconsistent with observed data, weak to moderate positive selection is consistent but unidentifiable if rare
statements.note: Data ruled out strong/frequent positive selection; weak-to-moderate positive selection stays possible but undetectable if rare.
